page: Amazon Web Services r6a.large is an entry-tier memory-optimized instance deployed on the AWS Nitro System. Hardware resources include 2 vCPUs mapped to a single dedicated physical core of an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. Memory capacity is set to 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, which equates to an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Hardware security and cryptographic extensions include AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, alongside basic AVX, though advanced extensions like AVX-512 and AMX are not supported. The instance has no integrated local storage and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight an asymmetric performance profile. The instance achieves strong results in single-core compute evaluations, demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 2989.68. It delivers average marks in single-threaded gzip compression at 28.84 GB/sec and Geekbench single-core testing at 1643.0. In contrast, multi-threaded operations are constrained by the single physical core architecture, resulting in low multi-core Geekbench marks of 2024.0 and reduced throughput on database operations and Redis SET testing. Uncached memory bandwidth tests record 31.33 GB/sec for reads and 21.46 GB/sec for writes.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, r6a.large serves as a low-overhead entry point for applications requiring substantial memory relative to compute capacity without paying for unneeded processor cores. Tradeoffs include the total reliance on network-attached storage, low baseline network throughput, and hardware limits on concurrent task processing. The instance profile is suited for small in-memory caches, lightweight relational databases, memory-bound microservices, and modest ETL data ingestion jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 2 vCPUs across 1 dedicated physical core and 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, establishing a high 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation. The server includes no bundled local storage and features a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI are available, while AVX-512 extensions are unsupported. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-core compute results alongside average compression throughput, though multi-core capacity and memory bandwidth metrics reflect its single physical core constraint. The configuration represents a resource-efficient option for workloads prioritizing memory capacity over parallel processing power, making it a functional deployment for small in-memory caching layers, modest database instances, and memory-bound background processing pipelines.
